requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: Docs state that diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly and must be fixed there. This matches the deliberate behavior in [L8] (metadata types are not analysed and the defining assembly owns validation), so it is consistent with the ledger and not a defect.

Receipts/PositionalRecordNullKeyDiagnosticTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 1/1 failed

findings.claim: `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null for a record's positional property, because that property's declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. The resulting diagnostic has `Location.None`, so the new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper discards it. Input: `[MessagePackObject] public partial record Cmd([property: Key((string)null)] string Scope);` declared in source. Base crashed here with an InvalidCastException; head now silently drops `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` for a type in the compiling assembly. The requirement says diagnostics should not crash on metadata symbols, not that source diagnostics may disappear.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.PositionalRecordNullKeyDiagnosticTests.PositionalRecordPropertyWithNullKey_ReportsBothKeysNullDiagnostic. It runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer on the positional record and expects a BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. On head no such diagnostic is reported.

findings.claim: The new tests only exercise the unkeyed-member path for a struct whose Key is a string property. No test covers the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) for a metadata type, so mutating or reverting that line is not detected. Also, the unkeyed-member test's MemberNeedsKey path is reachable only when diagnostics are not filtered, and the test passes whether the FirstOrDefault change is present or not if the wrapper drops the diagnostic anyway.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) -> ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because no test has a metadata generic struct with a property whose Key attribute has null int and string keys.

hunches.claim: The constructor now routes every analyzer diagnostic through `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`. That filter drops any diagnostic whose location is `Location.None`/null, not just diagnostics about metadata symbols. `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null whenever the property's syntax is not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, for example a positional record property whose syntax is a `ParameterSyntax`. So a source-declared positional record parameter with `[property: Key(null)]` would silently lose the MsgPack `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` error. The requirement asks that such diagnostics not crash; it does not ask that diagnostics on source symbols in the compiling project be suppressed. Ledger L8 only exempts metadata types.

receipt_plan.detail: Write a VerifyCS test (LanguageVersion.Latest, SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck) with a source-declared `[MessagePackObject] public partial record R([property: Key(null)] string A);` and expect the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic. On head it is expected to be missing, because GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null and the wrapper drops the diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source of the current compilation, including diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None). Previously, diagnostics like MsgPack004/MsgPack003 etc. that were created with a null/None location (e.g. via GetIdentifierLocation returning null) would be reported; now they silently vanish. It also drops diagnostics located in a syntax tree from another compilation. This is a global filter on all analyzer diagnostics, beyond the narrow crash fix, and could suppress diagnostics users currently see.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009/012/018 verifiers) at base and head; add a case where the diagnostic is created with a null location from a partial or source-declared type and assert it is still reported. Any test whose expected diagnostic disappears fails.

hunches.claim: The wrapper is applied only to reportDiagnostic, while the crash fix covers just two of the three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites. Line 735 (the reporter's first site) is not changed in this diff. If it is still reachable for a metadata closed generic struct, the IndexOutOfRangeException persists.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer/generator test with the repro (a referenced-assembly struct Item<T> used as Item<int> member in a [MessagePackObject]) and assert no CS8785/AD0001; also grep for remaining DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] in TypeCollector.cs.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation, including diagnostics with Location.None. Before this change those were forwarded. A diagnostic that legitimately has no location, such as one produced when GetIdentifierLocation returns null, would now be silently suppressed for source types too. This is a wider behavior change than the crash fix needs. Existing analyzer tests would be the way to check.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the full analyzer test suite (MsgPack003-018 tests). Add a case where a diagnostic is created with a null or None location for a source type and assert it is still reported.

hunches.claim: The wrapper ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation, including diagnostics with Location.None. No test checks that diagnostics for source-declared types are still reported. If the guard were broken (e.g. negated or removed) only the crash-path tests would notice. The negated version would suppress all analyzer diagnostics, but the visible tests in this diff only assert absence of diagnostics, so they would pass.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1447 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)) -> if (!(...)); expected to survive because all three new tests assert zero diagnostics, so suppressing every diagnostic still passes.

hunches.claim: The wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of the compilation, not only diagnostics on metadata types. Case: a source `[MessagePackObject]` class derives from a base class in a referenced assembly, and that base is not itself a MessagePackObject. A public base property without [Key] makes MemberNeedsKey (and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) fall back to a null location, and the diagnostic is then dropped. The defining assembly never validates that base, because it is not a MessagePackObject there. So no assembly reports the MsgPack004 error, and generation proceeds for an invalid source type. Ledger L8 covers types that are themselves from metadata, not source types that inherit metadata members.

receipt_plan.detail: Read ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (TypeCollector.cs:1444-1450) together with line 1077, where `item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` is null for an inherited metadata property. Location.None is not IsInSource, so the diagnostic is discarded. Confirming it needs a two-compilation test: emit a lib with `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }`, then analyze `[MessagePackObject] public class D : Base {}` and check for MsgPack004.

hunches.claim: The new README section 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' and the MsgPack004 doc addition are conventions-neutral, but the README says closed generics from referenced assemblies 'can be used', which promises no formatter in the consuming assembly. The requirement expects a generated resolver, not a formatter for the closed type. The wording is slightly ambiguous about whether the consuming assembly generates a formatter. Reading the docs against the generator output would show this.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the README wording with the generated resolver output in the new tests, which only assert that the resolver hint name exists, not that it contains a formatter for MyGenericStruct<int>.

hunches.claim: The third crash site fixed at line 1101 (MemberNeedsKey, FirstOrDefault()) is hit only if the member lacks a key and is public. The 'UnkeyedMember' test covers it, but reverting to [0] while keeping the wrapper is never tested for AOTDerivedKeyAttribute (derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax) for a metadata type. That branch is unguarded and untested.

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:1076 derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken) on a metadata attribute would still throw; no test uses a derived KeyAttribute on a type from a referenced assembly.

hunches.claim: The resolver-generation assertion checks only that the hint name exists. It does not verify the resolver content registers the closed generic formatter, nor that the closed generic type is handled correctly. The requirement asks for a generated resolver, so this is acceptable, but a resolver that omits the member silently would pass. The test duplicates the generator run with different compilation settings (Net80 vs test framework), so the second run may not match the verifier's behavior.

receipt_plan.detail: Assert.Contains(expectedResolverHintName, hintNames) only checks the hint name; reading the helper shows no assertion on generated text.

hunches.claim: The first and third tests use LanguageVersion CSharp7_3 and a class MyObject, not the record/init shapes from the repro. The record struct test is the only one covering the reporter shape. The init-accessor path (MsgPack017 near the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull site) is not exercised for metadata types.

receipt_plan.detail: Tests 1 and 3 define Content/Key as get/set; only test 2 uses init, and no test has a metadata generic struct with an init property with initializer.
